The test image shows a tomato compound leaf with:
- General yellowing/chlorosis across all leaflets
- Brown marginal necrosis (leaf edge burn/scorch)
- Small scattered dark spots on some leaflets
- Wilted/drooping appearance

This pattern suggests vascular or bacterial disease. Top candidates: Verticillium Wilt, Bacterial Canker, Early Blight. Let me view reference images across 8 classes.

**Analysis summary:**

- Test image: tomato compound leaf branch with **general chlorosis** (pale yellow-green), **prominent brown marginal necrosis** (leaf edge scorch), and **scattered small dark spots**
- Bacterial Canker (Bugwood_1): strong match — marginal necrosis/scorch + scattered spots on leaves, similar pattern
- Bacterial Canker (Bugwood_17): severe wilt with brown dried margins — advanced stage
- Verticillium Wilt: similar yellowing/wilting but less pronounced marginal scorch
- Early Blight: concentric ring spots — no match
- Late Blight: large dark water-soaked lesions — no match
- Septoria: small circular spots with halos — no match
- Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus: severe plant-wide wilting/bronzing — no match
- Leaf Mold: pale patches on upper surface — no match

The test image most closely matches **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato** — the combination of marginal scorch, scattered small spots, and leaf chlorosis on a branch is characteristic. Bugwood_1 reference is the closest visual match.
